theorem actualExtendedThirdRetainedCellKernel_eq_indicator {e : ℝ} {m : ℕ}
    {j : ActualExtendedThirdDyadicLabel m} (hj : j ∈ actualExtendedThirdRetainedCells e m) :

declarations.name: actualExtendedThirdRetainedCellIntegral_sum_uniform_approx
declarations.signature:
theorem actualExtendedThirdRetainedCellIntegral_sum_uniform_approx {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ e₀ : ℝ, 0 < e₀ ∧ e₀ ≤ 1 / 384 ∧ ∃ m₀ : ℕ,
      ∀ e : ℝ, 0 ≤ e → e ≤ e₀ → ∀ m : ℕ, m₀ ≤ m →
        |(∑ j ∈ actualExtendedThirdRetainedCells e m, actualExtendedThirdRetainedCellIntegral e m j) -
          actualExtendedThirdIdealFunctional| ≤ ε

mathematical_findings.detail: RetainedCellKernel is the indicator of the actual Ico OwnedCell times the actual CapKernel evaluated at that cell actualPhysicalLevel. For retained j, finiteLevel_on_cell first identifies the actual finite lookup value; only afterward is the nonlinear CapKernel evaluated. Thus RetainedCellKernel equals indicator OwnedCell FiniteKernel as a function on the whole tuple space, without a lower-sieve-function linearization.

If a retained owner exists, its kernel is the original finite kernel and every other retained summand vanishes by actualOwnedCell_unique. If no retained owner exists, actualFiniteLevel_outside gives precisely the old buffered level; the two lower-factor arguments coincide, so CapKernel is zero pointwise, including possible zero denominators under total real division. This proves the exact finite sum for all real e and every t, without null-wall or positivity hypotheses.

For e in [0,1/384], the prior full-domain FiniteKernel integrability is a theorem. Multiplying it by the measurable actual cell indicator yields IntegrableOn RetainedCellKernel on the original closed ordered domain. The separate CapKernel-on-cell theorem follows through integrable_indicator_iff and the exact nested restriction identity. No per-cell integrability is supplied by the caller.

The real cell integral is over actualOwnedCell inter actualClosedOrderRegion rho, with the original physical cell level and original coordinates. integral_indicator at the restricted full-domain measure, then Measure.restrict_restrict, gives exactly that intersection order. No unsupported claim that the full owned cell lies in the original domain is needed.

The actual pointwise finite kernel sum is substituted under the original full-domain integral. Current integral_finsetSum applies using the internally proved integrability of every retained cell kernel. The original FiniteFunctional is therefore exactly the finite sum of actual cap integrals. Only a finite sum is interchanged; no infinite sum, limit, density assumption, or uniform integrability premise appears.

The final uniform approximation invokes the existing FiniteFunctional uniform theorem whose IdealFunctional is the literal unbuffered original manuscript closed-old-cube functional. Its threshold e0<=1/384 supplies the range needed by the exact finite-sum identity. Rewriting that identity transfers the same epsilon bound to all later e,m; it does not assume convergence of individual cells as their number grows.
